answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may vote or claim rewards. A Sybil attacker must fund every identity separately, tying up capital across the jetty, knoll, and ocean of the network rather than multiplying influence for free. If identities are caught coordinating fraud, the protocol slashes their deposits; honest agents can challenge suspicious clusters, so creating many disposable accounts becomes both costly and risky.
